reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster because it incorporates more targeted workouts designed to build speed and strength, crucial for trail running. It includes tempo runs, hill repeats, and a dedicated cross-training session, all of which directly address the physiological demands of trail running. Plan B, conversely, focuses almost entirely on easy runs and recovery, which, while important, won't significantly improve speed or power. While Plan B’s emphasis on recovery is valuable, Plan A’s structured approach is more aligned with the goal of becoming a faster runner.
